use_case.title: YouTube — context engineering walkthrough
use_case.topic: context engineering walkthrough for LLM apps
use_case.target_audience: AI builders watching short-form technical walkthroughs on context engineering
use_case.notes: YouTube video. Adapter operates on title / description / tags / chapter timestamps / pinned-comment / end-card text only — voice profile = direct-and-ephemeral. No auto-publish; artifact is a copy-paste checklist mapped to YouTube Studio fields.

recommendation.diff_summary: Apply atomic-snippet-density via pinned_comment on the YouTube video (voice=scripted-and-timestamped).
recommendation.rationale: A pinned comment with a structured Q→A block is treated as a citable atomic snippet by ChatGPT/Perplexity transcript ingestion.

recommendation.diff_summary: Apply semantic-anchor-stability via chapters on the YouTube video (voice=scripted-and-timestamped).
recommendation.rationale: Chapter labels are the only stable anchors YouTube exposes to engines; stable wording across iterations keeps citations re-resolvable.

recommendation.diff_summary: Apply q-shaped-subhead-lattice via title_rewrite on the YouTube video (voice=scripted-and-timestamped).
recommendation.rationale: Engines will quote the title verbatim when answering; phrasing it as the user's question raises retrieval probability.

recommendation.diff_summary: Apply cross-engine-intermediary via description_structure on the YouTube video (voice=scripted-and-timestamped).
recommendation.rationale: The description's link block is YouTube's only outbound-citation surface; an authority-link block gives Perplexity a citation chain.

recommendation.diff_summary: Apply inverted-retrieval-target via description_structure on the YouTube video (voice=scripted-and-timestamped).
recommendation.rationale: Putting the citable answer in the first 200 chars of the description inverts the page so engines extract it before the metadata trail.

application.artifact_summary:
